statement:
You are given an array `lists` of `k` linked lists, each sorted in ascending order.

Merge all of them into a single sorted linked list and return its head. If there are no nodes at all, return an empty list.

examples.explanation: All eight values, taken together in sorted order.

why.d: Checks an empty `lists` and an input with nothing to return.

examples.explanation: There is one list, and it is empty.

why.d: Checks the smallest possible input and an input with nothing to return.

constraints: lists[i] is sorted in ascending order.
The sum of lists[i].length will not exceed 10⁴.
hints: The next output node is always the smallest among the current heads of the `k` lists.
A min-heap keyed by node value gives that smallest head in O(log k); alternatively merge lists pairwise, divide-and-conquer style.
Push every non-empty head into the heap; repeatedly pop the minimum, append it to the result, and push its `next` if it exists.

why.d: Checks lists that are all identical.

variants.title: Merge k sorted arrays
variants.approach: Min-heap of (value, array, index) · O(N log k)
variants.statement: Given `k` integer arrays, each sorted in non-decreasing order, return **one sorted array** containing all of their elements (duplicates kept).
hints: The next output is the smallest among the k current fronts.
Keep those fronts in a min-heap keyed by value.
Pop the smallest, then push the next element from the same array.

why.d: Checks an empty `arrays` and an input with nothing to return.
Checks the smallest possible input and an input with nothing to return.

solutions.name: Concatenate and Sort
solutions.description: Pour every element into one array and sort it, ignoring that the inputs were already sorted.

solutions.name: Min-Heap of (value, array, index) (Optimal)
solutions.description: Seed a min-heap with the first element of each non-empty array. Repeatedly pop the smallest, append it, and push the next element from the same array.

code.python:
import heapq

def mergeKArrays(arrays):
    heap = [(arr[0], i, 0) for i, arr in enumerate(arrays) if arr]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    out = []
    while heap:
        val, i, j = heapq.heappop(heap)
        out.append(val)
        if j + 1 < len(arrays[i]):
            heapq.heappush(heap, (arrays[i][j + 1], i, j + 1))
    return out

variants.title: k-th smallest overall
variants.approach: Min-heap, pop k-1 times · O(k log m)
variants.statement:
Given an array of sorted linked lists and an integer `k`, return the **k-th smallest value** (1-indexed, counting duplicates) across all lists, **without merging everything**.

`k` is at most the total number of nodes.
hints: Only the first k merged values matter.
Seed a min-heap with each list head.
Pop k - 1 times (pushing successors); the heap top is the answer.

solutions.name: Collect and Sort
solutions.description: Copy every value from every list into one array, sort it, and index the (k-1)-th element.

solutions.name: Min-Heap, Pop k-1 Times (Optimal)
solutions.description: Put the head of every list in a min-heap. Pop the smallest node k-1 times, pushing its successor each time; the heap top is then the k-th smallest.

solutions.name: Compare All Lists
solutions.description: At each step, find the minimum head across all k lists and append it to the result.
keyPoints: Scan all k heads to find minimum each time
n is total number of nodes
Simple but slow for large k

solutions.name: Divide and Conquer (Optimal)
solutions.description: Merge lists pairwise, reducing k lists to k/2, then k/4, etc. Like merge sort.
keyPoints: Each round processes all n nodes once
Reuses the merge two sorted lists subroutine
